7. [Maximum mark: 15]

A lighthouse, L, is located 8 kilometres due East of a coastguard station, C, on a straight stretch of coastline.

The coastguard station sees a Jet Ski, J, on a bearing of 062° and at a distance of 5.5 kilometres. This is shown on the following diagram.

[Diagram: Points C (coastguard) and L (lighthouse) on a horizontal coastline, with C to the left of L, distance 8 km. Point J is located inland such that the bearing from C to J is 062° and CJ = 5.5 km. North arrow shown at C. Triangle CJL is unlabelled except sides and angle. Diagram not to scale.]

(a) Find JL. [4]

While travelling due South, the Jet Ski breaks down at point B, before it reaches the coastline. The position of the Jet Ski at B and the lighthouse are shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram: Points J and B on a north-south line (due south direction), with B south of J. Lighthouse L at top of a 60-metre tower. The angle of depression from L to B is 0.94°. Diagram not to scale.]

From the top of the 60-metre-tall lighthouse, the angle of depression to the Jet Ski at B, is measured to be 0.94°.

(b) Find BL. [3]

The bearing from the Jet Ski at B to the lighthouse is 121°.

(c) Find the bearing from L to B. [2]

The jet-skier sets off a distress flare which is seen at the lighthouse and the coastguard station at the same time.
The lighthouse has a small rescue boat which travels at a speed of 48 km h⁻¹.

(d) Find the time, in minutes, for the lighthouse rescue boat to reach the Jet Ski at B. [2]

The coastguard rescue boat travels at a speed of 55 km h⁻¹ and sets out at the same time as the lighthouse rescue boat.

(e) Determine which rescue boat reaches the Jet Ski first. Justify your answer. [4]
records.independentSolutionText: (a) ∠JCL=90°−62°=28°. Using cosine rule: JL²=5.5²+8²−2(5.5)(8)cos28°=30.25+64−77.699=16.551, JL=4.06824…≈4.07 km. (b) tan(0.94°)=60/BL, so BL=60/tan(0.94°)=3656.85…m≈3.66 km. (c) Bearing from L to B is 301° (or N59°W). (d) Time=3.65685/48×60=4.57106…≈4.57 min. (e) Using cosine rule in triangle CBL: BC²=3.65685²+8²−2(3.65685)(8)cos31°=27.2200, BC=5.21728…km. Coast guard time=5.21728/55×60=5.69158…≈5.69 min. Since 4.57<5.69, the lighthouse rescue boat arrives first.

records.accessibleText: Solve the simultaneous equations, showing all working: (3x/2) + 5y = 5; 4x − 3y = 46.
records.independentSolutionText: Multiply the first equation by 2: 3x + 10y = 10. Multiply the second equation by 3: 12x − 9y = 138. Eliminate y by multiplying the first result by 9 and the second by 10: 27x + 90y = 90 and 120x − 90y = 1380. Adding gives 147x = 1470, so x = 10. Substitute into 4x − 3y = 46: 40 − 3y = 46, hence y = −2.

[2] (b) Write down the other two solutions of z³ = c, giving your answers in the form a + bi, where a, b ∈ ℝ. [2] (c) Find the solutions of (iz)³ = c, giving your answers in the form a + bi, where a, b ∈ ℝ. The solutions of (iz)³ = c can be represented on an Argand diagram by three points A, B and C. (d) Find the area of the triangle ABC. [2]
records.independentSolutionText: One root of z³=c is z=-2+2√3 i = 4 cis(2π/3). Cubing gives c=64 cis(2π)=64. The other cube roots are 4 cis(0)=4 and 4 cis(4π/3)=2-2√3 i. For (iz)³=c, write iz=4 cis(2kπ/3); then z=-i(iz), giving the three points A=2√3+2i, B=-2√3+2i and C=-4i (equivalently the corresponding Argand coordinates). These form an equilateral triangle of side 4√3 and altitude 6, so area = (1/2)(4√3)(6)=12√3 square units.

[Maximum mark: 15] Consider the function f(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d, where x ∈ ℝ and where a, b, c and d are real constants. The graph of f has a point of inflexion at (−2, −2c + d + 24). (a) Show that a = 3/2 and b = 9. [6] It is given that the tangents to the graph of f at x = −3 and x = k are horizontal. (b) (i) Show that c = 27/2. (ii) Find the value of k. (iii) State whether f has a local maximum or a local minimum at x = k, justifying your answer. [7] The graph of f intersects the y-axis at the point P. (c) Show that the tangent to the graph of f at x = −3 passes through P. [2]
records.independentSolutionText: Write f(x)=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d. Since the inflection point has x-coordinate −2, f''(−2)=0: −12a+2b=0, so b=6a. Its y-coordinate condition gives f(−2)=−2c+d+24. But f(−2)=−8a+4b−2c+d=16a−2c+d, hence 16a=24 and a=3/2, b=9. (b)(i) The horizontal tangent at x=−3 gives f'(−3)=0. Since f'(x)=3ax^2+2bx+c, 27a−6b+c=0, so c=27/2. (ii) f'(x)=(9/2)x^2+18x+27/2=(9/2)(x+3)(x+1), so the other horizontal tangent is at k=−1. (iii) f''(x)=9x+18, so f''(−1)=9>0; therefore f has a local minimum at x=−1. (c) The y-intercept is P=(0,d). At x=−3, f(−3)=d, and f'(−3)=0, so the tangent there is horizontal, hence its equation is y=d and it passes through P.
